## Purpose and Scope

This Reference Architecture Document (RAD) provides **illustrative** architecture patterns, logical component descriptions, technology considerations, and governance framework implementation guidance that support realization of the normative capabilities defined in the parent Architecture Building Block:

**[GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-2.9.01 — AI Data Security & Privacy](../GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-2.9.01.md)**

> **Informative Content Notice**: **Technology choices** in this document are **illustrative**, not mandated. Vendor product names, specific frameworks, and configuration values are examples of how the parent ABB's capability characteristics *may* be realized — they are not mandated choices. Implementation teams select specific technologies appropriate to their context, subject to standard enterprise procurement, security review, and governance processes.
>
> **The security control patterns themselves reflect the normative SHALL/SHOULD/MAY requirements of the parent ABB** ([GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-2.9.01](../GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-2.9.01.md)). Platform engineers should treat those patterns as required design outcomes even though the specific technologies used to achieve them are a team decision.

## Platform Engineering Scope

> **Reading guide for platform engineers**: This section answers the three highest-priority questions before you engage with the detailed patterns below: where your scope ends relative to the INFRA ABB, which controls you own vs. which other teams own, and which normative requirements from the parent ABB translate directly to platform configuration work. The subsequent sections provide implementation patterns for each area.
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#data--infra-boundary]

### DATA / INFRA Boundary

This ABB governs the **data layer** of AI systems — what is stored, how it is classified, protected, de-identified, versioned, cataloged, and audited. The sibling ABB **[GUID-SEC-AI-INFRA-2.9.03 — AI Infrastructure & Platform Security](../GUID-SEC-AI-INFRA-2.9.03.md)** governs the **compute substrate**: MLOps platform hardening, GPU/TPU cluster isolation, container and Kubernetes security, ML CI/CD pipeline gates, and secrets management for AI credentials.

The boundary runs at the `Training Environment Data Binding` interface defined in the parent ABB: the DATA capability provisions secured, de-identified datasets *to* the training environment; the INFRA capability governs the training environment *itself*. Both ABBs apply to an AI platform team — consult them together for the complete control set governing an end-to-end MLOps platform.

### Control Responsibility Matrix

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Network isolation (private subnets, no public endpoints) | **Owns** | Reviews / validates | — | — |
| RBAC/ABAC enforcement on training data stores | **Owns** (mechanism) | Reviews | Owns (role definitions, access approvals) | — |
| Data loss prevention (DLP) enforcement | Shared | **Owns** (policy definition) | — | — |
| Tamper-evident audit log delivery | **Owns** (log sources) | Owns (SIEM ingestion, alerting) | — | — |
| De-identification pipeline (technical execution) | **Owns** | — | Owns (method approval, validation) | — |
| Privacy budget tracking (differential privacy) | **Owns** | — | Owns (budget policy) | — |
| Training data catalog (tooling and storage) | **Owns** | — | Owns (governance, stewardship process) | — |
| Access provisioning and periodic access reviews | Supports (tooling) | — | **Owns** (data stewards) | — |
| Anomaly detection / UEBA alerting | Enables (log sources) | **Owns** | — | — |
| Model privacy testing (membership inference) | Participates | **Owns** | — | — |
| Privacy impact assessments (PIAs) | — | — | **Owns** | Owns |
| Data use agreements (DUAs) | — | — | Owns | **Owns** |
| AI data privacy incident response | — | **Owns** | Participates | Participates |

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#technical-controls-requiring-platform-implementation]

### Technical Controls Requiring Platform Implementation

The following normative requirements from the parent ABB translate directly to platform-owned configuration or pipeline engineering. Process controls owned by Privacy/Governance or GRC (PIAs, DUAs, data stewardship) are excluded from this list.

**Data protection** (parent ABB Principle 2):
- Implement encryption at rest using enterprise-approved cryptographic standards; key management SHALL use a centralized, access-controlled key management service (not per-service or per-team keys)
- Implement RBAC and ABAC on training data stores; access SHALL be scoped to specific AI projects and roles — not blanket organizational access
- Place training data in isolated network zones with restricted ingress and egress; no direct internet-accessible endpoints on training data stores
- Integrate training data pipelines with enterprise DLP; configure automated blocking of unauthorized exfiltration paths (large transfers, unapproved destinations)
- Deliver comprehensive, tamper-evident audit logs of all data access events to the enterprise SIEM: minimum fields are principal identity, resource accessed, action, timestamp, and source network location
- **Audit log retention**: configure training data access logs for a minimum **6-year retention** period (HIPAA administrative requirement, 45 CFR 164.530(j)) with tamper-evident storage and access controls preventing modification or premature deletion

**De-identification pipeline** (parent ABB Principle 3):
- Build a de-identification pipeline stage that executes approved methods — at minimum HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier removal, augmented by statistical analysis — before datasets are promoted to the training data repository
- Store a de-identification run record (method applied, parameters, date, responsible party, k-anonymity result or equivalent) alongside each dataset version in the training data catalog

**Privacy-preserving ML** (parent ABB Principle 4):
- Platform SHALL be capable of supporting differential privacy training (DP-SGD or equivalent) for model training jobs on high-risk or high-sensitivity datasets; privacy budget consumption SHALL be tracked and enforceable per dataset
- Platform SHOULD support federated learning execution patterns where data cannot be centralized; this is a SHOULD, not a SHALL — document the decision if not implemented
- Synthetic datasets SHALL be validated for training data memorization before being promoted to the training data repository

**Monitoring and detection** (parent ABB Principle 7):
- Configure SIEM alert rules for anomalous access to training data stores: triggers include unusual query volume, access outside defined business hours, access from unexpected network locations, and access by principals not assigned to an active AI project
- Integrate with enterprise DLP alerting for large-scale data transfers originating from training environments
- Build model privacy testing (membership inference attacks, and where feasible model inversion) into the model validation gate before any model is promoted to production; results SHALL be evaluated against documented acceptable thresholds
- Automate detection of training data access where no current, executed DUA exists for the accessing user/project; route violations to the data steward review workflow

### Pattern 1: AI Data Ingestion & Collection Layer

**Capability**: Secure and privacy-compliant acquisition of data from source systems into AI data repositories.

**Key Concerns**: Ensuring data in transit is protected; verifying consent status at ingestion; tagging data with provenance and permitted purpose; applying minimal retention at the ingestion layer.

**Illustrative Technology Approaches**:

- **Transport Security**: TLS 1.3+ for all data in transit; mutual TLS where source systems support it (e.g., clinical integration engines, claims processing systems)
- **API Security**: OAuth 2.0 or client certificate authentication at ingestion endpoints; rate limiting to prevent abuse
- **Input Validation**: Schema validation and sanitization at the ingestion boundary to prevent injection attacks
- **Provenance Capture**: Metadata tagging at ingestion capturing source system, collection timestamp, consent basis, and original purpose (supports lineage requirements from parent ABB Principle 5)
- **Consent Verification Integration**: Pattern — query an enterprise consent service or data governance platform at ingestion to flag records lacking documented AI/ML use consent; route consent-unknown records to a holding queue pending review

---
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#pattern-2-de-identification--anonymization-pipeline]

### Pattern 2: De-identification & Anonymization Pipeline

**Capability**: Transform identifiable data into de-identified or anonymized datasets suitable for AI training in a repeatable, validated, and audited manner.

**Key Concerns**: Satisfying HIPAA Safe Harbor and Expert Determination requirements; AI-specific re-identification risk (quasi-identifier linkage, model inference); structured vs. unstructured data treatment; audit trail of de-identification operations.

**Illustrative Technology Approaches**:

- **Unstructured Data (Clinical Notes, Free Text)**:
  - NLP-based PHI detection and redaction tools. Examples: AWS Comprehend Medical, Microsoft Text Analytics for Health, Microsoft Presidio (open-source), Philter (open-source, clinical NLP)
  - Pattern: identify → classify → mask/replace with synthetic placeholder → validate residual PHI rate

- **Structured Data (Claims, Enrollment)**:
  - Remove HIPAA Safe Harbor 18 identifiers as baseline
  - Generalize quasi-identifiers: age → age ranges; exact date → year or date-shifted value; ZIP → 3-digit prefix or suppressed if population <20,000
  - Apply k-anonymity analysis using tools such as ARX Data Anonymization Tool or equivalent statistical tooling
  - Date shifting: randomize dates by a consistent per-patient random interval, preserving relative temporal relationships for AI models

- **Re-identification Risk Assessment**:
  - After de-identification, calculate k-anonymity level for the dataset
  - Simulate linkage attacks against known external datasets (e.g., public demographic data)
  - Expert Determination: for complex or high-value datasets, engage a qualified statistical expert to assess re-identification risk per HIPAA 45 CFR 164.514(b)(1)
  - Document method, parameters, and validator in the de-identification audit record

- **Governance Integration**: De-identification audit records (method applied, parameters, date, responsible party) are stored alongside the dataset version in the training data catalog.

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#pattern-3-ai-training-data-repository]

### Pattern 3: AI Training Data Repository

**Capability**: Centralized, secured, governed storage for AI training, validation, and test datasets with immutable versioning, least-privilege access, and privacy tagging.

**Key Concerns**: Encryption at rest and key management; network isolation; RBAC/ABAC enforcement; dataset versioning and immutability; privacy budget tracking for differential privacy use cases.

**Illustrative Technology Approaches**:

- **Data Lake Storage**: Object storage in a cloud data lake (examples: AWS S3, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, Google Cloud Storage) or on-premises equivalent, placed in a private network zone with no direct internet access
- **Encryption**: AES-256 at rest with customer-managed keys (CMK) via cloud KMS services (examples: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault); key rotation policy enforced
- **Network Isolation**: Training data lake in private subnets (VPC/VNet) with restrictive security groups/firewall rules; no public endpoints; VPC endpoints or private link for service access
- **Access Control**:
  - Role-based access control (RBAC): project-scoped roles (e.g., `ai-project-x-scientist`, `ai-project-x-reader`)
  - Attribute-based access control (ABAC): access decisions incorporate data classification tags (PHI, de-identified, synthetic) and user attributes (project membership, clearance level)
  - Time-bound permissions: access grants tied to specific AI projects expire when project closes
- **Dataset Versioning**: Immutable dataset versions upon creation; changes create new versions; version history maintained in data catalog; lineage traces back to source data and de-identification run
- **Audit Logging**: All bucket/container access logged to centralized audit log platform (examples: AWS CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, Splunk); alerts configured for suspicious access patterns (anomalous volume, off-hours access, unexpected principals)
- **Privacy Budgets**: For datasets used with differential privacy training, track cumulative epsilon (ε) expenditure per dataset; enforce privacy budget limits before permitting additional use

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#differential-privacy-dp]

#### Differential Privacy (DP)

**What it provides**: Mathematically provable privacy guarantees that limit what an adversary can learn about any individual from model outputs or training data releases.

**Illustrative libraries and frameworks**: Opacus (DP for PyTorch), TensorFlow Privacy, IBM Diffprivlib, Google's DP Library

**Usage patterns**:
- **DP-SGD (Stochastic Gradient Descent)**: Apply differentially private training via gradient clipping and calibrated noise addition; use when training models on sensitive data where model memorization is a risk
- **Aggregate statistics releases**: Apply DP when publishing aggregate statistics from sensitive datasets to prevent inference attacks
- **Synthetic data generation with DP**: Use DP-GAN or similar approaches to generate synthetic datasets with formal privacy guarantees

**Privacy budget guidance**: Set epsilon (ε) in consultation with a qualified privacy technologist. Published guidance (NIST and academic references) provides context: lower ε values provide stronger privacy at some utility cost; higher ε values preserve more utility with weaker guarantees. Epsilon values SHALL be documented with explicit justification and approved per the AI data governance process.
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#federated-learning-fl]

#### Federated Learning (FL)

**What it provides**: An architectural approach to distributed model training where client organizations train locally on their own data and share only model updates (gradients), not raw data.

**Illustrative frameworks**: TensorFlow Federated, PySyft, Flower (flwr), OpenFL

**Usage patterns**:
- **Multi-organization collaboration**: Training a shared model on data from multiple state Medicaid agencies or health plans without centralizing data
- **Privacy-sensitive on-premises data**: Training on hospital EHR data that cannot leave the clinical network
- **Architecture**: A central aggregation server coordinates training rounds; clients receive the global model, train locally for one or more rounds, and transmit gradient updates (not data) back; server aggregates gradients using secure aggregation to prevent individual client exposure

**Practical considerations**: Data heterogeneity across clients (non-IID distributions) affects model convergence; federated training is slower than centralized; gradient inversion attacks exist and should inform secure aggregation design.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#synthetic-data-generation]

#### Synthetic Data Generation

**What it provides**: Artificially generated datasets that preserve statistical properties and patterns of real data without containing information about real individuals.

**Illustrative tools**: Synthea (healthcare-specific synthetic patient generation), Gretel.ai, Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), DataSynthesizer, CTGAN

**Usage patterns**:
- **Development and testing**: Use synthetic data when real data is unavailable or too sensitive for development environments
- **Third-party sharing**: Provide synthetic datasets to vendors, researchers, or model development partners who cannot receive real PHI
- **Training data augmentation**: Supplement limited real datasets with synthetic records to improve model performance

**Validation requirement**: Synthetic data generation models must be tested to confirm they do not memorize real records (membership inference testing against the generative model). Synthetic data utility should be validated by comparing distributions and model performance on real vs. synthetic training.
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#secure-multi-party-computation-smpc-and-trusted-execution-environments-tees]

#### Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) and Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs)

**What it provides**: Methods for performing computations on sensitive data where no single party sees all inputs (SMPC), or where data is protected within hardware-isolated secure enclaves during processing (TEEs).

**Illustrative technologies**:
- SMPC: CrypTen (Facebook/Meta), TF Encrypted, OpenMined PySyft, SCALE-MAMBA
- TEEs: Intel SGX, AWS Nitro Enclaves, Azure Confidential Computing, AMD SEV
- Homomorphic Encryption: Microsoft SEAL, HElib, TFHE

**Usage patterns**:
- SMPC: Collaborative analytics or joint model training on datasets from multiple organizations where contractual or regulatory constraints prevent any party from seeing other parties' complete data
- TEEs: Protecting sensitive data during inference (data is loaded into a secure enclave; even the host OS/cloud provider cannot read it); useful for highly sensitive inference scenarios

**Trade-offs**: Performance overhead is significant for both SMPC and homomorphic encryption; TEEs add operational complexity. These patterns are appropriate for high-sensitivity, high-value use cases where standard security controls are insufficient.

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#pattern-5-data-governance--policy-enforcement]

### Pattern 5: Data Governance & Policy Enforcement

**Capability**: Automated enforcement of data use policies, access controls, and retention rules; centralized training data discovery and cataloging.

**Illustrative Technology Approaches**:

- **Training Data Catalog**: Centralized metadata registry for all AI training datasets. Examples: Collibra, Alation, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Azure Purview, Apache Atlas (open-source). Key metadata: dataset name/ID, purpose, data sources, sensitivity classification, de-identification status, k-anonymity level, retention policy, access controls, lineage graph, version history, privacy budget consumed.

- **Access Request Workflow**: Self-service data discovery portal for data scientists; governed access request workflow routed to data stewards for approval; time-bound access provisioning integrated with IAM.

- **Policy Engine**: Attribute-based access control engine making real-time access decisions based on data classification, user attributes, and environmental attributes. Examples: Open Policy Agent (OPA), AWS IAM conditions/SCPs, Azure ABAC.

- **Dynamic Data Masking**: Column-level masking applied dynamically for query-time access in lower environments or exploratory access tiers; highly sensitive fields (e.g., SSN, MRN) masked unless user has explicit unmasked access. Examples: database-native masking features, Apache Ranger, Databricks Unity Catalog.

- **Privacy Budget Enforcement**: For differential privacy workflows, track cumulative ε consumption per dataset per release cycle; deny training requests that would exceed approved privacy budget.

---
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#pattern-6-privacy-monitoring--compliance]

### Pattern 6: Privacy Monitoring & Compliance

**Capability**: Active monitoring of AI data stores and deployed models for privacy risks; compliance reporting; privacy incident detection.

**Illustrative Technology Approaches**:

- **Model Privacy Testing**:
  - Membership Inference Attack Testing: run automated membership inference attacks against deployed models (tools: ML Privacy Meter, Adversarial Robustness Toolbox (ART)); alert if attack success rate exceeds documented threshold
  - Model Inversion and Attribute Inference: periodic penetration testing using established ML privacy attack toolkits
  - Privacy Metrics Dashboard: track differential privacy budgets consumed, k-anonymity levels maintained, re-identification risk scores, and membership inference attack success rates

- **Data Access Auditing**:
  - Centralize training data access logs in enterprise SIEM (examples: Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, AWS Security Hub)
  - UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) rules to detect anomalous access: bulk downloads, access outside business hours, access from unexpected network locations, access by users not assigned to an active AI project
  - Quarterly access reviews by data stewards; automated reports of users with access to training data; revoke inactive access automatically after defined period

- **Data Exfiltration Detection**:
  - DLP policy integration: policies preventing upload of training data files to personal cloud storage, external email, or removable media
  - Network monitoring: alerts on large outbound data transfers from AI training environments

- **Compliance Reporting**:
  - Automated generation of HIPAA security rule compliance evidence for AI data: audit logs demonstrating access control enforcement, encryption configuration reports, access review completion records
  - Privacy KPI dashboard reported to appropriate governance stakeholders: percentage of AI projects with completed PIAs, number of privacy incidents, DP/FL adoption rates, SLA on PIA completion

---

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#data-lifecycle-security-patterns]

## Data Lifecycle Security Patterns

The following sections describe security and privacy patterns for each phase of the AI training data lifecycle.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#phase-1-data-collection--sourcing]

### Phase 1: Data Collection & Sourcing

**Objective**: Secure and privacy-compliant acquisition of data for AI purposes.

**Key Activities**:

1. **Consent Verification**: Confirm data subjects consented to AI/ML use; document consent basis (treatment, research, explicit consent)
2. **Data Minimization**: Collect only data required for defined AI use case; avoid "collect everything" approach
3. **Provenance Documentation**: Record source system, collection date, consent status, original purpose; maintain in lineage metadata
4. **Secure Transfer**: Use encrypted channels (TLS 1.3+, SFTP with strong ciphers) for data transfer from source systems to the AI data platform
5. **Access Logging**: Log all data ingestion operations for audit

**NIST SP 800-53 Controls Applied**:
- SC-8: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
- AC-3: Access Enforcement at ingestion endpoints
- AU-2/AU-12: Audit logging of data collection activities

**NIST Privacy Framework Controls Applied**:
- PR.PO-P1: Organizational privacy values and policies established
- ID-IM-P4: Data processing purposes documented

---
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#phase-2-data-curation--de-identification]

### Phase 2: Data Curation & De-identification

**Objective**: Transform raw data into privacy-safe training datasets.

**Key Activities**:

1. **Data Quality Assessment**: Validate completeness, accuracy, and consistency; remove duplicates and errors
2. **De-identification Execution**: Apply HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination; implement k-anonymity analysis, quasi-identifier generalization, date shifting (see Pattern 2 above)
3. **Unstructured PHI Redaction**: Apply NLP-based PHI detection and redaction for clinical notes and free-text fields (illustrative tools: AWS Comprehend Medical, Microsoft Presidio, Philter, ARX)
4. **Quasi-Identifier Generalization**: Generalize age, ZIP codes, dates of service to reduce re-identification risk
5. **Re-identification Risk Validation**: Calculate k-anonymity level; simulate linkage attacks; document risk assessment results
6. **Dataset Versioning**: Store de-identified dataset as an immutable version with provenance linking to source data and de-identification run record

**NIST SP 800-53 Controls Applied**:
- SC-28: Protection of Information at Rest (encrypted storage during curation)
- MP-6: Media Sanitization (secure deletion of intermediate identifiable artifacts)

**NIST Privacy Framework Controls Applied**:
- PR.DS-P6: Disassociation of data from individuals
- PR.PO-P2: Privacy roles and responsibilities established
- ID-RA-P1: Privacy risk assessments conducted

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#phase-3-training-data-storage--access-management]

### Phase 3: Training Data Storage & Access Management

**Objective**: Secure, governed storage of AI training datasets with least-privilege access.

**Key Activities**:

1. **Encrypted Storage**: Store training data in an encrypted data lake (AES-256, customer-managed keys in enterprise KMS)
2. **Network Isolation**: Place data lake in private network zones; no direct internet exposure; service endpoints only
3. **RBAC/ABAC Configuration**: Implement role-based and attribute-based access controls; access scoped to specific AI projects with time-bound permissions
4. **Dataset Cataloging**: Register datasets in training data catalog with full metadata (classification, purpose, retention, lineage, de-identification status)
5. **Data Use Agreements**: Require executed DUAs before access to PHI-derived training data is provisioned; DUAs specify permitted use, retention, and security obligations
6. **Periodic Access Reviews**: Quarterly reviews of training data access by assigned data stewards; revoke unused or expired access

**NIST SP 800-53 Controls Applied**:
- AC-3: Access Enforcement (RBAC/ABAC)
- AC-2: Account Management (provisioning, reviews, revocation)
- SC-28: Protection of Information at Rest
- SC-7: Boundary Protection (network segmentation)
- AU-2: Audit Events (log all access)

**NIST Privacy Framework Controls Applied**:
- PR.AC-P1: Access to data minimized and managed
- PR.DS-P1: Data protected commensurate with risk
- CT.DM-P1: Data access monitored and reviewed

---
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#phase-4-model-training--data-in-use]

### Phase 4: Model Training & Data in Use

**Objective**: Protect data during model training; prevent privacy leakage into trained models.

**Key Activities**:

1. **Isolated Training Environments**: Execute model training in isolated compute environments (dedicated network segments, no external network egress during training)
2. **Ephemeral Data Access**: Provide data scientists with temporary, project-scoped access to training data; access automatically expires after the training run or project closure
3. **Differential Privacy in Training**: For high-risk data classifications, apply DP-SGD (differentially private stochastic gradient descent) to provide formal privacy guarantees for trained models (illustrative libraries: Opacus for PyTorch, TensorFlow Privacy)
4. **Model Privacy Validation**: Test trained models for privacy leakage before promotion to any shared or production environment: membership inference, model inversion
5. **Training Log Sanitization**: Ensure training logs and experiment tracking platforms do not capture or retain raw training data samples; sanitize logs before long-term archival (illustrative platforms: MLflow, Weights & Biases — configure to exclude data samples from logged artifacts)
6. **Secure Model Artifact Storage**: Encrypt saved model weights and configuration files at rest; access to model artifacts controlled separately from training data

**NIST SP 800-53 Controls Applied**:
- SC-7: Boundary Protection (isolated training environments)
- AC-6: Least Privilege (scoped training data access)
- AU-2: Audit Events (training job logging)

**NIST Privacy Framework Controls Applied**:
- PR.DS-P6: Disassociation techniques applied (DP)
- CT.DP-P1: Data processing monitored and audited

---
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#phase-5-inference--production-data]

### Phase 5: Inference & Production Data

**Objective**: Protect inference inputs and outputs; prevent model-based privacy leakage in production.

**Key Activities**:

1. **Input Validation**: Validate and sanitize inference inputs at the API boundary to prevent adversarial inputs designed to extract training data
2. **Rate Limiting & Throttling**: Apply rate limits to inference APIs to slow membership inference and model extraction attacks; alert on query volumes exceeding expected patterns
3. **Output Monitoring**: Monitor model outputs for potential PHI leakage; flag and review suspicious outputs (e.g., generated text containing apparent names, MRNs, or date-of-birth patterns)
4. **Inference Audit Logging**: Log inference requests and responses for audit purposes; sanitize logs to exclude any PHI present in inputs or outputs before long-term storage
5. **Query Pattern Anomaly Detection**: Detect and alert on systematic probing patterns (many similar near-identical queries indicating extraction or membership inference attempts)
6. **Model Versioning & Rollback**: Maintain versioned model registry; enable rapid rollback to previous model version if privacy leakage is detected in a production release

**NIST SP 800-53 Controls Applied**:
- SI-10: Information Input Validation
- SC-8: Transmission Confidentiality (TLS for inference APIs)
- AU-2: Audit Events (inference logging)

**NIST Privacy Framework Controls Applied**:
- CT.DP-P1: Data processing monitored
- RS.RP-P1: Response to privacy incidents prepared

---
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#phase-6-data-retention--deletion]

### Phase 6: Data Retention & Deletion

**Objective**: Comply with retention policies; honor individual deletion requests in the context of trained AI models.

**Key Activities**:

1. **Automated Retention Enforcement**: Configure lifecycle policies on training data storage to automatically delete datasets after the defined retention period (HIPAA minimum: 6 years for policies/procedures; project-specific retention documented in the DUA; default: 7 years for healthcare data unless shorter project retention applies)
2. **Deletion Request Handling** — three-tier approach:
   - **Immediate (raw data)**: Remove the individual's records from raw data stores and prevent inclusion in any future training runs
   - **Already-trained models (assessment-based)**: Document that the individual's data was part of the training set; assess whether model retraining is needed based on the proportion of training data affected, model type, and risk of inference; document the outcome and responsible approver
   - **Model retirement**: If deletion affects a material portion of the training dataset, consider retiring and retraining the model from a revised dataset
3. **Cryptographic Erasure**: Where technically feasible, use cryptographic erasure (delete encryption keys for the affected data) as an efficient secure deletion method for large encrypted datasets
4. **Multi-Pass Overwrite**: For on-premises or non-cloud storage where cryptographic erasure is not available, apply NIST-approved multi-pass overwrite methods
5. **Deletion Verification**: Audit log confirming deletion was completed across all data stores (primary, backup, logs, derived datasets) to the extent technically feasible
6. **Deletion Audit Record**: Maintain tamper-evident log of deletion requests received, actions taken, and any documented exceptions

**NIST SP 800-53 Controls Applied**:
- MP-6: Media Sanitization (secure deletion)
- SI-12: Information Management and Retention
- AU-2: Audit Events (deletion logging)

**NIST Privacy Framework Controls Applied**:
- PR.PO-P5: Data retention and disposal practices implemented
- ID-IM-P5: Individual rights accommodated (right to deletion)

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#ai-data-governance-oversight-structure]

### AI Data Governance Oversight Structure

A cross-functional oversight function is needed to govern AI data privacy practices enterprise-wide. The following describes a reference implementation pattern:

**Charter**: Oversight of AI data security and privacy practices; approval authority for high-risk AI data uses; resolution of AI data privacy policy questions.

**Recommended membership**:
- Privacy Officer (chair or co-chair)
- Enterprise Data Governance lead
- Information Security / CISO representative
- Legal / Compliance representative
- AI/ML Engineering lead or designate
- Business/Clinical representative for major AI use case domains

**Meeting cadence**: Monthly standing meetings; ad-hoc convening for urgent approvals or incidents.

**Key responsibilities**:
- Review and approve privacy impact assessments (PIAs) for all AI projects processing PHI or PII
- Establish and update AI data privacy policies (de-identification standards, retention policies, DP budget policies)
- Approve use of novel privacy-preserving techniques (e.g., first use of a specific FL framework or SMPC protocol)
- Review privacy metrics and incident reports
- Provide policy guidance on consent and patient rights in AI contexts
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#data-stewardship-for-ai]

### Data Stewardship for AI

**Assignment**: Assign a designated data steward for each AI training dataset or dataset family. Stewards are typically domain data owners with responsibility for the data's use in AI contexts.

**Steward responsibilities**:
- Classify new datasets; update classification when data content or use changes
- Approve or deny data access requests (in coordination with governance oversight for high-risk requests)
- Conduct quarterly access reviews; revoke unused or unjustified access
- Maintain lineage documentation for assigned datasets
- Monitor for policy compliance violations; escalate to governance oversight if needed
- Serve as the point of contact for privacy officer and legal inquiries about the dataset

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#privacy-impact-assessment-pia-process]

### Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) Process

**Trigger**: A PIA is required for all AI projects processing PHI, PII, or sensitive personal data before the project accesses or uses that data. PIAs are also required when an existing AI project materially changes its data use (new data sources, new output uses).

**PIA Template Coverage**:
The enterprise PIA template for AI projects should cover:
- Data sources and types (PHI, PII, aggregate, de-identified, synthetic)
- Legal basis and consent documentation for each data source
- De-identification and anonymization approach planned
- Data retention and deletion plan (including post-training model treatment)
- Privacy risks specific to AI: model inference attacks, training data re-identification, model memorization, output leakage, continuous learning drift
- Mitigation strategies selected (DP, FL, access controls, monitoring)
- Compliance self-assessment against HIPAA, applicable state privacy laws, and internal privacy policies

**Review and Approval**:
1. AI project team completes PIA using the standard template
2. Data steward for the relevant dataset(s) reviews and adds technical accuracy comments
3. Privacy Officer reviews PIA for completeness, adequacy of mitigations, and compliance assessment
4. Privacy Officer approves or requires changes; high-risk PIAs (models processing extensive PHI, high-stakes decisions, novel privacy-preserving techniques) are escalated to the AI Data Governance Oversight function for approval
5. Approved PIA is saved in the governance document repository and linked to the AI project record in the training data catalog

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#training-data-catalog-implementation]

### Training Data Catalog Implementation

**Purpose**: Centralized registry of all AI training datasets, enabling governed discovery, lineage visibility, and policy enforcement.

**Core metadata per dataset entry**:
- Dataset identifier (unique ID)
- Dataset name and description
- Data sources (linked to source system records)
- Sensitivity classification (PHI, de-identified, synthetic, aggregate)
- De-identification status (method applied, date, responsible party, k-anonymity level)
- Permitted purpose(s) for AI use
- Retention policy and scheduled deletion date
- Access controls in effect (roles/groups with access)
- Lineage graph (sources consumed, transformations applied, downstream models trained)
- Version history
- Privacy budget consumed (for datasets under DP constraints)
- Linked PIA record
- Data steward assignment

**Illustrative tooling**: Enterprise data catalog platforms such as Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview, or AWS Glue Data Catalog can serve as the backing platform for the AI training data catalog. The catalog instance or catalog domain for AI training data should be configured with appropriate access controls (not all enterprise staff should be able to see what AI training datasets exist).

**Self-service access requests**: The catalog should support a self-service data discovery workflow where data scientists can find available datasets and submit governed access requests routed to the appropriate data steward for approval.

[strategy/guidance/security/Artificial-Intelligence/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-AI-DATA-RAD-3.9.01.md#data-use-agreement-dua-framework]

### Data Use Agreement (DUA) Framework

**Purpose**: Contractual and internal governance instrument ensuring that access to PHI-derived AI training data is conditioned on documented obligations.

**When required**: A DUA is required for all access to AI training datasets derived from PHI, regardless of whether the data has been de-identified (de-identified PHI still warrants a DUA as an organizational governance control).

**DUA content elements**:
- Permitted AI use case(s) (specific project; no secondary use without amendment)
- Authorized individuals / roles with access
- Access period (expiry date; renewable with steward review)
- Security obligations (encryption in transit and at rest, no copying to personal devices or personal cloud storage, MFA required)
- Retention and deletion obligations (delete local copies at project closure)
- Audit and inspection rights (organization reserves right to audit compliance)
- Incident reporting obligation (report unauthorized access or suspected breach within defined timeframe)

**Process**: Electronic acknowledgment of DUA terms as part of the access provisioning workflow; annual recertification for long-term or ongoing access; DUA terms enforced through access revocation if violated.
